main_text.p: quosdam; vel, Transire faciens, Removens, ut Chaldæus & Aben Esra interpretantur, Prov.25.20. Chald. Transire fecit, Amovit, Transtulit, Abstulit: Præter. הֶעֱדִיו מִנּוֹ[?] Amoverunt ab eo, Daniel.5.20. Particip. מְהַעֲדִיר[?] Transfert, Dan.2.v.21. Futur. יְהַעֲדוּן[?] Transferent, Dan.7.26.

masc. Ornatus, Ornamentum: Item, Osoris: In pausa est cum Sægol: עֲדִי[?] וְאֶעְדֶךָּ עֲדִי[?] Et ornavi te ornamento, Ezech.16.11. וַתֵּבְאִי בְּעָדִי עֲדִיִּים[?] Et pervenisti in ornatum ornamentorum, Ezech.16.7. id est, ad summum ornatum: כְּעֲדִי תִלְבָּשִׁי[?] Tanquam ornamento vestieris, Jesa.49.18. Aff. עֶדְיִי[?] Os ejus, Psal.32.9. Ornamentum suum, Exod.33.v.4. עֶדְיְךָ[?] Os tuum, Psal.103.5. Plur. עֲדִיִּים[?] ut ante.

עֲדִיִּים[?] m.p. Remotiones: Res inquinatæ & abominabiles, quæ Removentur & abjiciuntur: וּכְבִגֶד עֲדִים[?] Et sicut pannus remotionum, Jesa.94.6. id est, abjectissimus, vulgò Pannus menstruatus, is enim abjici solet; Significationem hanc habet juxta Chaldæum & R.Salom. sed formam à defectivis, quasi ab עדד[?].
עֲדוּת[?] Ornamentum regium; 2.Reg.11.12. Aliam significationem vide in עוד.

עַד Usque, Usque ad, Donec, Dum, Adhuc, ac notatur eo, tam loci quàm temporis quidam Transitus: עַד עוֹלָם Usq; in seculum, Psalm.18.51. עַד מָקוֹם Usq; ad locum Sechem, Genes.12.6. עַד הֱיוֹתִי Usq; esse me, Jon.4.2. id est, Adhuc existente me, cùm adhuc essem: עַד זֹאת מְדַבֵּר Adhuc isto loquente, Job.1.18. תַּמְתּוֹן עַד Donec moriamini, Jesa.22.14. Adjunguntur ipsi & aliæ particulæ: עַד פֹּה Donec veniat, Gen.49.10. עַד אֵם Idem, Jesa.30.17. עַד אֲשֶׁר נֶעְבַּר Donec transeamus, Numer.20.17. עַד מֶה vel מֶה עַד Usquequò? עַד מָתַי Idem, עַד אַן Quousque? עַד כֹּה Hucusq;, Eousq;: עַד הֵנָּה Hucusq;: Unde

page.notes: Hebrew and Greek forms are transcribed from a low-resolution scan; the Hebrew vowel points and several pointed forms are uncertain and are marked [?]. The running head ע is the Hebrew letter at the top centre. "Jesa.94.6." is printed as such (probably for Jes. 64.6), kept as printed. "sunin" and "funin" in the Aff. entry are read as printed; the scan is unclear there. The line "Unde" at the foot is the last full line and continues on the next page.
